resources.string: Couldn\'t refresh your inbox. Showing the copy saved on this device.
Don\'t open it unless you\'re sure where it goes, and never enter a password or personal details there.
Only open it if you trust where it goes.
Some links in this email may lead to a fake or harmful website. Don\'t open the links marked with a red ✕.
Some links in this email look unusual. Tap one marked with a yellow ! to see why before anything opens.
The link is written in an unusual way that real companies rarely use, a common trick to hide what it does or where it goes.
The link\'s text shows one website, but it takes you to another. Fake emails do this to look trustworthy.
The connection to this website isn\'t secure, so anything you type there, like a password, could be seen by others.
The website\'s name imitates a well-known one with a small change, a trick fake websites use.
The link is shortened, so you can\'t see where it really goes before you open it.
Your network sends this link somewhere other than where it should go. Someone may be redirecting you to a fake website.
Trustmail couldn\'t make a secure connection to this website, so it can\'t confirm the website is real.
This website was created very recently. Fake websites are often only a few days or weeks old.
This part of the website was set up very recently, which can mean someone else just added it.
The website\'s security certificate is for a different name, so it may not be the website it claims to be.
The website\'s security certificate comes from an unusual provider, which is rare for real companies.
Gmail confirmed that this email really comes from the address it shows.

Gmail couldn\'t confirm that this email really comes from the address it shows. That\'s often harmless, but someone could be pretending to be this sender. Be careful if it asks you to do something or to share information.

This email pretends to come from an address that didn\'t send it, so it\'s probably a fake. Don\'t open its links or reply with personal details. If it claims to be from someone you know, contact them another way.
You\'ve exchanged emails with this address before.
This is the first email you get from this address. If it asks you to do something or to share information, be careful before you continue.
Trustmail couldn\'t check whether this address has emailed you before, for example because you\'re offline. Be careful if it asks you to do something or to share information.
Lets scripts inside an email run. Scripts can change what you see after Trustmail has scanned the links, so leave this off unless an email needs it. Applies the next time you open an email.

Suspicious links in an email\'s footer (unsubscribe, privacy policy, social media) don\'t count toward the email\'s verdict. They still get a badge and a warning when you tap them, and an unsafe footer link still counts. Applies the next time you open an email.
Trustmail checks every email for phishing before you act on it.
Preview: an email with a safety mark next to each link and a warning at the top
Trustmail checks who really sent it and scans every link in it.
A green, yellow or red mark sits next to each link, and anything wrong is explained at the top of the email.
Risky links ask you to confirm before they open.
On the next step you\'ll sign in with your Google account, so Trustmail can read your Gmail.
